messages:
maria_sales: Hey folks — HaloHealth POC asking for Private deployment network checklist. They prefer PrivateLink but worried about split-horizon DNS, egress IPs, and preserving client source IP through our connector. Also asked for quick pricing compare (PrivateLink vs VPC peering) and firewall rules. Can we give a short bundled answer they can consume?

sam_netops: Short answer: PrivateLink = interface endpoints in customer VPC. Good for security (no internet path) but the traffic terminates in our VPC so client source IP will be the connector/NAT IP unless they use some passthrough architecture. Split-horizon DNS is usually handled by a private hosted zone or resolver forwarding.

kevin_sales: Pricing note: interface endpoint charges are on customer's cloud bill plus our Private deployment licensing. Peering avoids endpoint charges but requires cross-account peering or TGW and has different failure modes. I'll pull the specific $/hr numbers to include.

dev_infra: Firewall / SG snippet we send usually looks like: 
```
# allow outbound to Redwood interface endpoints
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0abcd1234 --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.0.0.0/16
# if customer uses NAT egress to internet for callbacks open 443 to our egress IPs/FQDNs
```
Also advise customers to allow TLS SNI to pass through any TLS-inspecting proxies.

jess_eng: Quick technical add: if they need true client src IP preservation for requests all the way to model containers, peering + NAT mapping on their side or a direct private circuit (DX/ER) into a dedicated VPC is the reliable path. PrivateLink rewrites src.

maria_sales: Can we put together a 1-pager: (1) recommended topology for typical hospital POC, (2) firewall/SG snippet, (3) expected pricing buckets. I want to send by EOD.

sam_netops: For split-horizon DNS options:
- Option A: Customer creates a Route53 private hosted zone for redwood-inference.internal and points API records to the interface endpoint ENIs.
- Option B: Customer forwards queries for our service domain to our Route53 Resolver endpoints.
- Note: Windows clients behind corporate proxies may need explicit proxy bypass rules for the endpoint IPs.

dev_infra: Sample allowlist FQDNs/ports to give them: 
```
FQDN: api.redwood-inference.com (or region-specific: api.us-east-1.redwood-inference.com)
Ports: 443 outbound (HTTPS)
Optional: 123/udp to nearest NTP if they block time sync (recommend allow)
IP ranges: we provide a small set of egress IPs for Private deployments; will confirm exact list per-region.
```

kevin_sales: I'll confirm price ranges: endpoint charge (AWS) + our connector monthly fee + egress GB rate. If they commit to Dedicated capacity we can rebate some connector fees.

maria_sales: Security questionnaire asks about SOC2, key management, and data-at-rest. Quick answers?

jess_eng: SOC2: we provide SOC2 Type II report to enterprise customers under NDA. KMS: we support customer-managed keys in Private deployments (bring-your-own-KMS) for encryption at rest. Data residency: we can pin region and offer on-prem package if required.

deploy-bot: ticket INF-4321 created for 'HaloHealth POC - private-deploy network checklist and pricing' assigned to @kevin_sales and @sam_netops.

sam_netops: Action items from my side: 1) confirm exact egress IP CIDR per region, 2) provide route53/private-hosted-zone example and resolver endpoint snippet, 3) test curl flow with sample cert behavior behind TLS-inspectors. ETA 3pm PT.

kevin_sales: Action items: confirm pricing + draft one-pager. I'll include options: PrivateLink small infra cost, peering + TGW recommended for src-IP preservation, Dedicated reserved capacity pricing. ETA EOD.

maria_sales: Perfect — I'll assemble and send to HaloHealth. If anything changes ping me in-thread. Thanks! :+1:
